What aspects of a game contribute most to getting/keeping you immersed in its world?

I'm a big fan of RPG elements that allow me to have a character that is unique instead of the same everytime I play it also adds replayability to the game. Many that do have it tend to add options for you to reset and redo the character, and while I can appreciate fixing a misclick but rebuilding the whole thing over again after maxing it out means you would have one setup for leveling and another for end game, kind of weird for a character to suddenly not only have a new way of doing things but be unable to do the old one. I'm also odd in that I prefer not to be able to max everything out as it makes each character unique instead of leading to the same end every time.

Pacing is important for me. Too big of a sudden jump and I remember I'm playing a game. A story has to move slowly enough to feel like one cohesive world instead of a series of missions, but fast enough to keep from getting monotonous.
